lines.source: old lab film, scene 1: an answer that arrives after the system needed it; told as a tracking task
lines.text: A robot hand has to stay under a moving ball. An AI watches the ball and tells the hand where to go. But what if its answer comes too late?

lines.source: old lab film, scene 1: a fixed-rate controller gets the same budget every cycle
lines.text: The hand is run by a controller, and the controller works on a beat. Many times a second it must move. It can never skip a beat.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 1: inference time is variable
lines.text: The AI keeps its own pace. Most answers come back quickly. A few take much longer, and nobody knows in advance which.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 2: blocking inference misses deadlines
lines.text: So suppose the controller waits for every answer. Each slow answer costs it beats. The hand freezes, and the ball gets away.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 2: a separate worker proposes, the controller never waits
lines.text: Better: never wait. The controller keeps its beat, and simply uses the latest answer the AI has finished.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 3: on time, but using an answer about a world that has changed
lines.text: Nothing is late now. But during a slow answer, the latest one gets old. It describes where the ball was, not where it is.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 3: timestamp checked before use, fallback when a proposal expires
lines.text: So every answer carries the time it was made. When it is too old, the controller stops trusting it, and does something safe instead, like stopping.
That is the whole idea. The AI advises. The controller keeps the clock.

lines.source: Simplex architecture (Sha, IEEE Software 2001) guards complex controllers with simple ones; open part: large models with variable inference time
lines.text: Engineers already build safety-critical systems this way. The open problem is doing it for today's large AI models, and proving the timing really holds.
AI will keep getting smarter. The beat will never wait for it.
